sources.title: TSMC, Samsung commit to ASML's newest chipmaking tools as AI drives demand

brief.headline: TSMC and Samsung have committed to buying ASML's advanced High NA EUV chipmaking machines, securing the manufacturing roadmap for next-generation AI and memory chips.

event.summary: TSMC and Samsung committed to using ASML's High NA EUV lithography machines and joining an initiative for 12-inch photomask technology to improve productivity and lower costs.
event.magnitudeBasis: The commitment involves machines costing around $400 million each from the world's two largest chipmakers, providing critical growth visibility for ASML.

chain.mechanism: TSMC and Samsung commit to using ASML's $400 million High NA EUV machines and a new 12-inch photomask initiative to lower chipmaking costs and improve productivity.
TSMC's adoption of High NA EUV secures the advanced manufacturing capability needed for the complex transistor architectures of future AI chips designed by Nvidia and AMD.
Intel already uses High NA EUV. TSMC and Samsung joining as customers validates the technology but erodes Intel's exclusive lead in next-gen manufacturing.
Samsung's commitment to use High NA EUV for DRAM from 2028 and 2030 to extend scaling and efficiency increases competitive pressure on rival memory makers like Micron.

exposures.rationale: Nvidia designs advanced AI GPUs and relies on TSMC for manufacturing. TSMC's commitment to ASML's next-gen lithography ensures the foundry capacity and technical capability required for Nvidia's future complex transistor architectures.
AMD designs advanced CPUs and GPUs and competes in AI accelerators. Like Nvidia, it relies on TSMC's foundry services and benefits from TSMC upgrading its manufacturing capabilities to High NA EUV.

Intel was the early adopter of High NA EUV. While TSMC and Samsung's commitments validate the technology, they also mean Intel will face direct competition using the same advanced tools, eroding its early-mover advantage.

Micron competes with Samsung in the DRAM market. Samsung's plan to use High NA EUV for DRAM from 2028 and 2030 to lower costs and improve efficiency could force Micron to make similar expensive capital investments or face a cost disadvantage.

watchAtOpen: ASML stock price at the US open to see if the positive adoption news offsets early flat-to-lower trading in Amsterdam.
TSMC (TSM) and Intel (INTC) share price reactions to gauge how the market values the shifting competitive landscape in advanced foundry tech.
Micron (MU) trading to see if memory investors react to Samsung's long-term DRAM scaling roadmap.
falsifiers: If TSMC or Samsung delay or cancel their plans to adopt High NA EUV machines.
If the high cost of the machines (around $400 million each) makes advanced chip production unprofitable for foundries.
If Intel's early deployment of High NA EUV fails to yield any competitive manufacturing advantages before TSMC and Samsung adopt it.
unknowns: The exact number of High NA EUV machines ordered by TSMC and Samsung.
The specific timeline for TSMC's deployment of the machines, as only Samsung's 2028 and 2030 targets are detailed.
Whether Micron plans to adopt High NA EUV or stick to alternative scaling methods for its DRAM.

quotes.text: Samsung and TSMC, the world's two biggest chipmakers, have committed to using ASML's High NA extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines, as demand grows for more advanced chips.
This tool can cost around $400 million.
Samsung, one of the world's biggest memory chipmakers, said it would use ASML's machines to produce DRAM, a key type of memory, from 2028.
